title: Derive GET /bff/jobs list surface metadata from canonical owner reads

summary.problem: In base 034e5a5f02dde88ceb96936f056304ff8c4afc97, GET /bff/jobs read canonical owner job rows via read_store.list_jobs_bff(...) and then built meta.surfaces.job_list via read_surface_meta('jobs', 'job_list', ...) without canonical owner results or diagnostics; the router never called read_store.get_degraded_sources() and ReadSurfacePorts has no such getter, so the observed old bug was legacy ReadSurfacePorts.dataset_source('jobs') == 'missing' (status='unavailable', source='missing'). Meanwhile, JobReadPort.get_degraded_sources() stored mutable last-call state on the port instance, which was a cross-request concurrency risk avoided by passing a per-call diagnostics dict.
solution: JobReadPort.list_jobs_bff collects healthy_sources and degraded_sources in call-local variables and populates a caller-supplied per-request diagnostics dict with exact same-invocation healthy_sources and degraded_sources.
ReadSurfacePorts.list_jobs_bff forwards status, job_type, diagnostics, and **kwargs to self.job_read.list_jobs_bff.

services/control-plane/bff/jobs/router.py passes a request-local diagnostics dict into read_store.list_jobs_bff(...) and computes meta.surfaces.job_list and meta.degradation via _owner_job_list_meta strictly from same-call diagnostics without row_sources/jobs compatibility fallbacks or TypeError fallback shims.

Single healthy owner resolves source to healthy_sources[0] and multi-owner composition resolves source to 'bff_composed' with status='ok' (or status='degraded' with degraded_sources and meta.degradation.reason when partial failures occur); missing or empty healthy_sources in same-call diagnostics fail closed to status='unavailable', source='unavailable', and has_data=False without falling back to legacy dataset_source('jobs') or inferring health from fake rows; concurrent list_jobs_bff calls do not leak diagnostics across requests.
